posts.title: Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why
posts.summary: People have been talking to each other for at least 100,000 years, as best we can tell. And in all that time, there has been only one thing in the world that could learn a human language to perfect fluency: a human child.  Now there are two.  Four short years after the release of ChatGPT,…
bullets: Current LLMs require roughly 100,000 times more data to achieve linguistic fluency than a human child, highlighting a massive inefficiency in current AI scaling paradigms.
With frontier models now training on trillions of tokens, the industry faces a looming 'data wall' where high-quality, easily available human-generated data may be exhausted as early as the 2030s.

The reliance on massive datasets for model performance is becoming a strategic bottleneck, forcing researchers to pivot toward reverse-engineering human cognitive development to achieve better results with less data.

Closing the data efficiency gap is now a critical objective for AI architects, as future model improvements will likely depend on architectural innovation rather than simply increasing the volume of training data.

posts.title: Xiaomi unveils 3-nm Xring D100 smart-driving chip, plans commercial use in 2027
posts.summary:
Xiaomi said the Xring D100 is China's first high-computing-power smart-driving chip built on a 3-nm process and can run models with up to 200 billion parameters locally.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi has unveiled the Xring D100, China's first 3-nm high-computing-power smart-driving chip, capable of running 200-billion-parameter models locally.
The chip has completed validation and is slated for commercial deployment in 2027, marking a significant step in Xiaomi's vertical integration strategy.
Xiaomi has invested over 21 billion yuan in its chip development program, employing nearly 3,000 experts to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia.

posts.title: Leapmotor stays profitable in H1 as margin and cash flow weaken
posts.summary:
Leapmotor's first-half net profit rose to 210 million yuan ($30.95 million), marking its second consecutive half-year of profitability.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Leapmotor achieved its second consecutive half-year of profitability with a net profit of 210 million yuan, representing a 600% year-on-year increase.
Despite revenue growth of 57.2%, the company's gross margin narrowed to 11.7% due to rising raw material costs and shifts in product mix.
Free cash flow plummeted 83.7% to 140 million yuan, reflecting increased procurement spending and inventory stocking.
Overseas expansion is a critical growth engine, with exports surging 372.6% to account for 27% of total sales in the first half of 2026.

posts.title: Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below
posts.summary:
Chips are getting bigger, more modular, and much more capable as new innovations mix with existing processes and long-researched projects go mainstream.
The post Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Heterogeneous integration and multi-die assemblies have become essential for leading-edge servers and edge devices as traditional monolithic scaling hits physical and economic limits.
The shift is driven by the inability to pack sufficient compute power into a single reticle-sized die, necessitating a move toward chiplets to meet the performance demands of data-heavy AI workloads.

Agentic AI is further complicating design requirements by demanding a mix of CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators, requiring AI-driven validation tools to ensure manufacturability and testability.

Industry leaders are targeting two orders of magnitude improvements in performance-per-watt, a goal that requires a fundamental realignment of manufacturing processes, advanced packaging, and logic scaling.
